rows.selection_reason: With zero completed experiments, the priority is to establish a strong anchor configuration that maximizes the number of clean one-at-a-time comparisons available for subsequent experiments. config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) uses the simplest and most standard choices across all variable sub-dimensions: PCA as the baseline RNA encoder, ViT-L as a strong standard image encoder, avgpool as the simplest aggregation, and concat as the simplest fusion. This makes it a natural reference point: config_002 isolates the image encoder (resnet50 vs ViT-L), config_020 isolates fusion (weighted vs concat), config_041 isolates aggregation (transformer vs avgpool), config_050 isolates RNA encoder (scgpt vs PCA), and config_034 isolates RNA encoder (scvi_n200 vs PCA). Starting with this 'simplest full pipeline' also avoids conflating the effect of multimodal fusion with the effect of complex sub-choices, so that if performance is weak, a follow-up unimodal baseline (e.g., config_009 or config_018) can cleanly attribute the gap to fusion vs. individual modality quality. Under a limited budget, this single experiment reduces the most uncertainty about the overall pipeline while preserving the greatest number of informative next steps.

With only one completed experiment (config_001: multimodal, PCA RNA, ViT-L, avgpool, concat → 62.9% acc), the most critical uncertainty is whether the RNA modality actually contributes meaningful signal over the image modality alone. Config_009 (image_only, multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool) is a clean ablation: it keeps the image encoder, aggregation, and profile setting identical to config_001 while removing the RNA branch entirely. If image-only performance is close to 62.9%, it suggests PCA-based RNA features add little value and we should redirect budget toward image-side improvements or stronger RNA encoders. If image-only is substantially lower, it confirms multimodal fusion is worthwhile and justifies further investment in optimizing fusion/aggregation. This single experiment resolves the foundational question of whether the multimodal architecture is justified before spending budget on finer-grained fusion or encoder comparisons.

Evidence: config_001 (multimodal, pca_n2000, multiprofile, avgpool, concat) achieves 0.629 acc, while config_009 (image_only, multiprofile, ViT-L, avgpool) achieves only 0.332 acc. This large gap suggests RNA is the dominant signal, but we cannot yet quantify how much the image modality actually contributes to the multimodal model. Question: config_018 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) is the cleanest single-variable ablation of config_001—it removes only the image modality while keeping the same RNA encoder, profile setting, and aggregation. This directly isolates the image contribution. Why best: With only two experiments done, the highest-uncertainty design question is whether the image modality adds meaningful value or is largely redundant. The answer determines whether future budget should be spent optimizing image encoders/fusion or RNA encoders/aggregation. Combined with the existing image_only baseline (config_009), this gives both unimodal baselines needed to interpret all future multimodal results. No other single experiment reduces this fundamental uncertainty as efficiently.

Evidence: config_001 (multimodal, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) achieves 0.629 acc, only +0.038 over RNA-only config_018 (0.591), while image-only config_009 is weak (0.332). This suggests RNA dominates and the image contribution is modest, but it is unclear whether the modest multimodal gain is a ceiling or an artifact of the simple concat fusion. Question: config_020 is identical to config_001 except fusion is changed from concat to weighted, making it a clean single-variable test of whether the fusion strategy is bottlenecking the image signal. Why best next step: it directly isolates the fusion effect without confounding changes to encoder, aggregation, or profile setting. A positive result would justify investing in stronger image encoders or transformer aggregation; a null result would indicate the image contribution is inherently limited with current encoders, redirecting budget toward RNA encoder improvements (scgpt, scvi_n200). Either outcome sharply reduces uncertainty about where to focus remaining experiments.

Evidence: config_020 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) is our best at 0.6352 acc / 0.6183 F1, and weighted fusion clearly beats concat (config_020 vs config_001). RNA dominates (0.5907) while image alone is weak (0.3316), but the multimodal combination adds ~4-5 points over RNA-only. Uncertainty: We have only tested avgpool aggregation; transformer aggregation is completely unexplored and could capture richer cross-profile interactions. Question: Does transformer aggregation improve over avgpool when all other settings (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, weighted fusion, multiprofile) are held constant? Why this is best: config_022 is a clean single-variable extension of our best-performing config, isolating the aggregation effect. Under a limited budget, testing the most impactful unexplored design axis (aggregation) on top of the strongest known configuration maximizes information gain per experiment and directly builds on the strongest evidence we have.

Evidence: RNA is the dominant modality (rna_only acc=0.5907 vs image_only acc=0.3316), and the best multimodal config (config_020, acc=0.6352) uses pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted. We now know avgpool+weighted is superior to transformer+weighted (0.6352 vs 0.5856) and weighted beats concat (0.6352 vs 0.6287). Uncertainty: We have only tested one RNA encoder (pca_n2000) in the best-performing pipeline. Since RNA drives most of the signal, the RNA encoder choice is the highest-leverage untested design decision. Question: Does a learned variational RNA representation (scvi_n200) outperform a linear PCA reduction (pca_n2000) when all other components (imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) are held at their best-known settings? Why this experiment: config_007 is a clean single-variable swap against config_020 (only rna_encoder changes), isolating the RNA encoder effect. This is more informative than testing the image encoder (resnet50) because RNA contributes far more to performance, so understanding whether a learned encoder can push the RNA signal higher is the key question for improving the overall model under a limited budget.

The strongest finding so far is that scvi_n200 dramatically outperforms pca_n2000 in the multimodal setting (config_007: 0.7062 vs config_020: 0.6352), a ~7-point gap. However, we cannot yet tell whether this gain is intrinsic to the learned RNA representation or arises from a synergy between scvi_n200 and the image modality. Config_040 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) is a clean single-variable comparison against config_018 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool, acc=0.5907): only the RNA encoder changes. If rna_only+scvi_n200 approaches ~0.68-0.70, the gain is primarily from the RNA representation and the image modality adds little marginal value; if it stays near ~0.60, the multimodal combination is genuinely synergistic and worth further investment. This decomposition is critical for deciding where to spend remaining budget—on improving the RNA encoder, the image encoder, or the fusion—making it the highest-information experiment under the limited budget.

Evidence: scvi_n200 is the dominant driver of performance (config_007: 0.7062 vs config_020: 0.6352 with pca_n2000), and the image modality adds ~5.6 pts on top of the RNA-only scvi_n200 baseline (config_040: 0.6501). However, we have only tested one image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) with scvi_n200. Uncertainty: it is unclear whether the image contribution is encoder-specific or whether a lighter backbone like resnet50 captures comparable signal. This experiment (config_014: scvi_n200 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted) is a clean single-variable change from the best-performing config_007, isolating the image encoder effect while holding the RNA encoder, aggregation, fusion, and profile setting at their known-best values. It is the best use of the next budget slot because it either confirms imagenet_vit_l is necessary (justifying its compute cost) or reveals that resnet50 is sufficient (freeing the search to focus on other dimensions), and it directly informs whether the ~5.6-pt image gain is robust to encoder choice.

Evidence: scvi_n200 clearly outperforms pca_n2000 as RNA encoder (rna_only: 0.650 vs 0.591; multimodal+vit_l: 0.706 vs 0.635), and config_007 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted) is the current best at 0.706. However, scgpt as an RNA encoder is completely untested across all 8 experiments, leaving a major gap in our understanding of the representation landscape. Question: config_030 (scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted) is a clean single-variable comparison against config_007, differing only in RNA encoder. This isolates the effect of the scgpt representation while holding the best-known image encoder, aggregation, and fusion fixed. Why best next: Under limited budget, resolving where scgpt sits relative to scvi_n200 and pca_n2000 is critical—it determines whether we should invest further in scgpt-based configurations or concentrate remaining experiments on scvi_n200 variants (e.g., singleprofile, transformer aggregation). A clean A/B test here reduces uncertainty about a fundamental design axis more efficiently than testing a second-order interaction like aggregation choice, which already shows a consistent direction (avgpool > transformer).

All nine completed experiments use multiprofile, so the value of multiprofile versus singleprofile is entirely untested. The strongest configuration so far is config_007 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) at 0.706 acc. config_035 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l, singleprofile, weighted) changes only the profile setting relative to config_007 (aggregation becomes None as a natural consequence of single-profile), giving a clean A/B test of whether multiprofile aggregation contributes meaningfully. If singleprofile matches or approaches 0.706, it simplifies the pipeline and redirects future effort; if it falls well short, it confirms multiprofile is a critical design choice and justifies further multiprofile-specific tuning. Under a limited budget, resolving this high-level architectural question is more informative than fine-tuning fusion or aggregation within an already well-supported multiprofile setting.
